versions.html:
Spell construction

Choose a base spell, add compatible runes, then review it.

Runes change power, duration, complexity and stamina cost. Check the limits before assembling.

Controls depend on your keyboard, gamepad and camera settings. The in-game guide shows your current bindings.

Classic edition reference

These original pages describe classic mouse and keyboard controls. Use the guidance above for current settings and gamepad controls.

General information

To construct a spell, you'll need its keystone. Spell keystones determine what school of magic the spell belongs to, as well as its principle and initial properties.
You can construct a spell using only a keystone, or you can add runes which change the spell's properties.
You can use your own keystones and runes (assuming, of course, you have them) or you can buy them in the shop just like you buy any other item.

Note: You cannot construct spells that are too complex or demand too much stamina for any of your characters to use them. The maximum complexity and stamina you have available will be shown framed in separate lines below the slot your keystone is in.

Constructing spells

To construct a spell click on its keystone in your inventory (bottom bar) or in the shop (top bar). The keystone will be placed into the appropriate slot.
The slots reserved will then be highlighted with a flickering frame. The number of highlighted slots is equal to the number of runes you can insert into this spell. This number changes each time you add a rune to the constructor. To add a rune click on its picture in either your inventory or in the shop and it will go to the next available slot.
The keystone determines what runes can be used for this spell. Runes which cannot be used will be dimmed.

Note: you can't place any runes into the constructor until you've placed a keystone. If you take the keystone out of the constructor and put it back into your inventory or shop, all runes you've added will also be removed from their slots and returned to where they came from.

The properties of the spell you have constructed are shown in the left panel, including any additional properties added by the runes you have used. The lower part of the screen shows the total price of the spell. This includes the price of any articles you bought.

To construct the item click on the "V" button, to cancel click on "X".

Note: if you construct a spell and then deconstruct it immediately afterwards you'll still be charged for the constructing and deconstructing cost. Caveat Emptor!

Deconstructing spells

If you want to deconstruct a spell, click on it and it will appear in a constructor's slot. In the lower-left corner of the screen you'll see the total cost of deconstructing the spell.
If you remove the keystone from its slot in the constructor after you've deconstructed the spell, the runes contained in it will also be removed.
When you deconstruct a spell from the shop, we assume you have purchased it (sorry, shoplifting is another chapter), so the runes from the spell will go into your inventory.

To deconstruct a spell click on the "V" button
To cancel click the "X" button

Note: if you deconstruct a spell and then construct it immediately afterwards you'll still be charged for constructing and deconstructing.

Features

A composite spell is one made up of a keystone and more than one additional rune. This type of spell cannot require less energy than a similar spell which contains only the keystone. Thus, the rune "Extra Energy" can never be used alone. It's only useful for composite spells as it compensates for the increased energy needed by the additional runes.
